- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — apply downward bias of 2–5% to forecasted peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.30) and price is trending upward, model tends to overestimate — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30) over 3+ days, model often underestimates — add 3–5% upward bias to forecast mean.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias in 10–14 day horizons — if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.40 to -0.30) triggers model lag — delay forecast peak by 1–3 days and reduce magnitude by 5–10%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates near-term (first 7 days) — cap first 7-day forecast at 1–2% below true outcome if sentiment is volatile.
